traps_and_failure_modes: Calling getPriorityFeeEstimate or getRecentPrioritizationFees WITHOUT account keys returns the global market (~2,986 microlamports/CU measured) when the pump.fun local market is 100,002-535,714. This single mistake will make you lose essentially every contested race while believing your fees are correct.

Using Jito's tip_floor p75 (9,523 lamports measured live) as your tip target. It aggregates all network bundles including arbitrage spam and is 100-500x below what landed competitive pump.fun transactions actually pay (p90 = 3,000,000 lamports). Build your own program-scoped tip percentile tracker.

Priority fee is charged on the REQUESTED compute unit limit, not the consumed amount. Observed bots request 1,400,000 CU on pump.fun buys that consume 153,860. At 500,000 microlamports/CU that wastes 0.000623 SOL per attempt. Over 1,000 attempts/day that is 0.62 SOL/day burned for nothing.

Interpreting the 77.1% pump.fun failure rate as slippage failures. It is not — it is competitors' guard programs aborting cheaply at ~1-3k CU. If you naively raise slippage to 'fix' failures you convert cheap losses into expensive bad fills and hand the difference to sandwichers.

Setting a wide percentage slippage on a buy. Your slippage cap IS the sandwicher's maximum extraction budget. A 2500 bps degen_buy setting is an explicit offer to lose 25%. Compute an absolute minimum-out from observed reserves instead.

Broadcasting buys through a public/shared RPC sendTransaction. Solana has no public mempool, so sandwiching requires transaction visibility before execution — a leaky shared RPC or a colluding validator is exactly that leak. Buys must go through Jito bundles, Helius Sender with mev-protect=true, or a paid private relay.

Using a fixed Jito tip account. All 8 are hardcoded and widely used; picking one creates an account write-lock hotspot that serializes your transaction against every other bot using the same account. Randomize per transaction.

Jito's default rate limit is 1 request/second/IP/region. A bot that assumes it can spam sendBundle will get HTTP 429s during exactly the launch windows it cares about. Either fan across regions, use multiple IPs, or route through Helius Sender (50 TPS).

Using blockSubscribe for detection. It has documented stability problems on high-traffic programs — connection errors and silently skipped data. You will miss launches and not know it. Use Geyser transactionSubscribe with a program filter.
Sequential submit-then-fallback instead of concurrent fan-out. Each sequential hop costs a full RTT (~1 slot). By the time your second attempt goes out the mint is 400-800ms old and already sniped.

Shred-derived signals are PRE-EXECUTION. A transaction visible in shreds may still fail or be reordered. Acting on a shred signal without re-validating against confirmed state means you will sometimes buy into a launch that never actually happened.

Simulating the transaction before a snipe to size the CU limit. simulateTransaction costs a full network RTT you cannot afford in a race. Precompute per-venue CU constants offline (the measured distributions above are tight enough) and add a fixed margin.

Provider documentation drift. sol-trade-sdk's minimum-tip constants are already stale for at least two providers (Nozomi listed as 0.0001 when its docs say 0.001; Helius listed as 0.0002 when its docs say 0.001). Re-verify every minimum against live provider docs before production or your transactions will be silently deprioritized.

Single-provider dependency for detection. Provider incidents happen, and an outage during a launch window is a total loss of that opportunity with no partial credit. Run two independent detection feeds with signature dedup.

Vendor-published benchmarks (BlockRazor's own study naming BlockRazor the winner; shreder.xyz benchmarking competitor Helius) are marketing. Even BlockRazor's self-favorable numbers show only 30-40% first-arrival. Instrument your own per-provider, per-region win rate and reweight from that.

Assuming Helius LaserStream is or is not Yellowstone-compatible based on secondary sources — competitor pages claim it uses a proprietary wire format while Helius's own docs call it a drop-in replacement. This determines whether your existing yellowstone-grpc client code works. Verify against Helius docs directly before architecting around it.

Paying for Raw Shreds ($800-1,000/mo/IP) before the rest of the pipeline is sub-50ms. The 100-500ms shred advantage is invisible if you then spend 200ms on transaction construction or a cold TLS handshake. Optimize the pipeline first, buy shreds last.

Not accounting for the 4-slot leader run. If you miss the current leader you have ~1.6 seconds until the next one — enough time for a region-switched retry. Bots that blindly resubmit to the same endpoint waste that entire window.

Rigorous quantitative literature and dat.topic: Rigorous quantitative literature and data studies on memecoin returns (Solana/pump.fun primary; Base/BSC secondary) — base rates, survival, rug/wash fractions, trader profitability, and strategy backtests
Rigorous quantitative literature and dat.executive_summary: The published literature converges on a brutal set of base rates. Graduation (bonding curve completion, ~$69k mcap) has run between 0.2% and 1.8% of launches through most of 2024-2026, spiking to 4.7-6.7% only after pump.fun's BOOST mechanic launched in late July 2026 (vs ~0.84% in June 2026) — so graduation rate is a REGIME variable, not a constant, and any bot economics must be re-estimated monthly. Because pump.fun launch FDV is ~$4-5k and graduation FDV is ~$69k, the graduation rate is approximately P(~15x from block-0 price); that means the true unconditional base rate of a 15x is roughly 1%, and of a 5x-from-launch perhaps single-digit percent. No peer-reviewed paper publishes a clean 2x/5x/10x/50x/100x peak-multiple histogram — this is the single biggest gap in the literature, and I could not verify any such distribution; do not trust any number you see quoted for it. The best proxy is the MemeTrans/MELT dataset (41,470 fully-migrated Solana memecoins, Dec 2024–Mar 2025): within 20 minutes of migration, 60.26% of tokens trade below 0.2x of migration price, 73% below 0.4x, and only 5.20% never trade below migration price at all. That is the decisive number for any "buy at graduation" strategy. Survival is equally harsh: CoinGecko's 18.67M-token study (Jan 2024–Jun 2026) finds 68.67% record their last trade on launch day, 80.37% within one day, and only 4.55% are still trading after 90 days. Manipulation is the default state, not the exception: Solidus Labs flags 98.6% of ~7M pump.fun tokens as rug/pump-and-dump (only ~97k ever held >$1,000 liquidity) and 93% of 388,000 Raydium pools as soft rugs (median rug size $2,832); Marino et al. find 92.22% of tokens with ≥30 swaps show at least one 4-sigma dump event; MELT labels 84.13% of migrated tokens high-risk. Wash trading estimates disagree violently by chain and method — MELT measures 21.4% of pre-migration pump.fun transactions as wash trades, while Chainalysis's conservative heuristics find only 0.035-0.046% of ETH/BNB/Base DEX volume — treat the Solana figure as the operative one. Retail profitability sources also disagree sharply: CoinGecko (3.14M wallets, realized PnL, Apr 2026) reports 73.28% profitable, but its own methodology note admits it counts realized PnL only, excluding never-sold bags, which mechanically excludes the modal total loss; a Dune-based 90-day Solana DEX meme study (Aug 2026, 304,161 wallets) reports 6.25% profitable with median loss $120 and only 25 wallets above $10,000. The crypto.news 29.6M-wallet study (Aug 2024) is the best-calibrated middle ground: 37.6% positive PnL but only 0.76% above $1,000 and 0.046% above $10,000 — profits are extremely power-law concentrated. Galaxy's Oct 2025 report finds 12 of ~12.9M pump.fun tokens hold >55% of the $4.8B aggregate FDMC and that median Solana memecoin hold time collapsed to 100 seconds (from 300 a year earlier). Critically, the only published backtest-like result — MELT's model-guided top-100 selection — achieves 76% precision but still loses 26.64% on average, versus 60.71% for random selection. In other words, the best published ML on migration-time features converts a catastrophic loss into a merely bad one; nobody has published a profitable memecoin selection strategy. Fee math: pump.fun bonding curve costs 1.25% per side (0.95% protocol + 0.30% creator), PumpSwap scales 1.25% down to 0.30% by market cap, plus priority fees, Jito tips, and sandwich losses (~3% total cost on an unprotected 1 SOL Raydium memecoin swap vs ~0.7% protected). Budget 4-6% round-trip friction. At that friction, a 5x-target strategy with full loss on losers needs a 21.0% hit rate; a 10x target needs 10.5%; a 2x target needs 52.5%. Against a ~5.2% base rate of a migrated token not even dipping below entry, the naive strategies are not close, and the entire edge must come from selection (bundle/concentration/social features) and from exit discipline, not from directional exposure.

findings.claim: Pump.fun graduation rate is a regime variable ranging ~0.2% to ~6.7%, not a constant; treat it as a monthly-recalibrated parameter
findings.detail: Marino et al. (arXiv:2602.14860, Sept 1–Oct 1 2025): 4,338 of 655,770 tokens graduated = 0.63%. Kamat (arXiv:2607.02823, May 8–Jun 10 2026): 1,651 of 832,941 = 0.198% (Wilson 95% CI 0.189–0.208%) — BUT the author's own limitation note says the collector's effective coverage window was ~6 minutes not 24 hours, so this is a lower bound and NOT cleanly comparable to Marino's 0.63%. The Block (Feb 19 2026): weekly graduations 1.15% of launches, a 7-month high; historical peak ~2%, historical low ~0.5%. The Block (Jul 29 2026): after BOOST launched, graduation rate hit 6.7% on one Friday, 4.7% over the prior four days, 2.5% the week before, vs a June 2026 average of ~0.84%. arXiv:2512.11850 (Q4 2024): 'fewer than 2%'. crypto.news (Aug 2024): 33,683 of 1,883,578 = 1.79%. Solidus Labs (Jan 2024–Mar 2025): <100,000 of ~7,000,000 tokens ever held >$1,000 liquidity = ~1.4%.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Do NOT hardcode a graduation rate. Compute a trailing 7-day and 30-day graduation rate from your own indexer every hour and expose it as `regime.grad_rate_7d`. Gate strategy aggressiveness on it: if grad_rate_7d < 0.5% run in defensive/observe mode; if > 3% (BOOST-like regime) allow larger size. Alert on any >2x week-over-week change — that means the launchpad changed mechanics and every prior-fit model is stale.

findings.claim: Graduation is arithmetically equivalent to roughly a 15x from block-0 price, so P(15x from launch) ≈ the graduation rate ≈ 1%
findings.detail: Marino et al. state the graduation threshold is 115 SOL total in the curve (30 virtual + 85 real) at ~$69,000 FDV. Pump.fun initial FDV is ~$4,000-5,500. 69,000 / 4,500 ≈ 15.3x. Therefore the fraction of launches that ever 15x from the first-block price is bounded above by (graduation rate) + (a small number of tokens that pumped hard on-curve but stalled before 85 real SOL). Given graduation rates of 0.198%–1.79% (normal regimes) and 4.7–6.7% (BOOST regime), P(≥15x from launch price) is ~0.2%–2% normally.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Use grad_rate as your directly-measurable proxy for P(15x from launch). For a sniper that buys in the first few blocks, expected value per launch = grad_rate × (15x realized minus exit slippage) − (1 − grad_rate) × (loss on curve). At 1% grad rate and 15x, gross EV ≈ 0.15 − 0.99×L. With L=0.9 that is deeply negative. A block-0 sniper is only viable if you can (a) exit partially on the curve before graduation and (b) select launches with grad probability >5%.

findings.claim: The empirical post-migration outcome distribution: 60.26% of migrated Solana memecoins trade below 0.2x of migration price within 20 minutes; only 5.20% never trade below migration price
findings.detail: MemeTrans/MELT (arXiv:2602.13480), 41,470 memecoins that completed launchpad and migrated to DEX, Dec 1 2024 – Mar 1 2025, 200M+ transactions. min_price_ratio = min token price within 20 min post-migration / migration price. Distribution: [0.0–0.2) 24,988 (60.26%); [0.2–0.4) 5,265 (12.70%); [0.4–0.6) 3,315 (7.99%); [0.6–0.8) 2,991 (7.21%); [0.8–1.0) 2,756 (6.65%); ≥1.0 (never dipped) 2,155 (5.20%). Over 73% collapse below 0.4x of migration price within 20 minutes.
findings.actionable_for_bot: This is your prior for any buy-at-migration strategy. A naive market buy at migration has a 60% chance of being down 80%+ within 20 minutes. Two direct implications: (1) never market-buy at the migration tick without a selection model; (2) if you do enter post-migration, place a hard stop at -25% to -35% and accept that you will be stopped out on the majority of entries; sizing must assume L (loss on losers) ≈ 0.30 with stops that actually fill, or ≈0.85 if they don't. Also: use the 5.20% 'never dipped' cohort as your positive label for a supervised model.

findings.claim: Token mortality: 68.67% of pump.fun tokens record their last trade on launch day; 80.37% within one day; only 4.55% survive past 90 days
findings.detail: CoinGecko Research, 18.67 million tokens with nonzero trading, Jan 14 2024 – Jun 18 2026. Same day 12,825,175 (68.67%); 1 day 2,184,433 (11.70%); 2-3 days 770,249 (4.12%); 4-7 days 642,614 (3.44%); 8-14 days 460,697 (2.47%); 15-30 days 382,289 (2.05%); 31-60 days 337,931 (1.81%); 61-90 days 222,077 (1.19%); 90+ days 850,180 (4.55%). 'Lifespan' = calendar days between creation and last bonding-curve trade, so the 90+ bucket understates true survival for graduated tokens (post-graduation trades on PumpSwap/Raydium are not counted). Average launch rate >21,000 tokens/day. Corroborating: chainplay.gg reports ~10,417 launched vs ~9,912 defunct per 24h.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Your universe decays with a half-life measured in hours. Any feature computed on a >6h window is computed on a survivorship-biased sample. Build your training labels with an explicit observation window (e.g. all launches in [T, T+24h]) and include the dead ones. Operationally: a position held >24h in a non-graduated token is almost certainly unexitable — enforce a max-hold timer.

findings.claim: Time-to-graduation is measured in minutes, not hours — median ~4.4 minutes and ~457 bonding-curve swaps
findings.detail: Marino et al. (arXiv:2602.14860), Sept–Oct 2025: median time to graduation ~4.4 minutes from token creation; median ~457 bonding-curve swaps to graduation; distribution has a pronounced heavy tail. Kamat (arXiv:2607.02823), May–Jun 2026, within a 6-minute observation window: median 1.66 min, p90 2.80 min, max observed 5.98 min (truncated by the collector, so biased low). Galaxy Research (Oct 2025): median hold time for a Solana memecoin is 100 seconds, down from 300 seconds a year earlier.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Your decision latency budget is seconds. A model that needs 5 minutes of trade history to score a launch will have missed the median graduation. Design two scoring tiers: T+0 to T+30s (creation metadata, dev wallet history, socials, first-buyer identity) and T+30s to T+180s (curve velocity, unique buyer count, bundle detection). Set your max-hold default to ~100-300 seconds to match the market's actual holding period; anything longer is a deliberate deviation from the crowd that needs its own justification.

findings.claim: 98.6% of pump.fun tokens and 93% of Raydium pools show rug / pump-and-dump patterns; median soft rug size is $2,832
findings.detail: Solidus Labs 2025 Rug Pull Report, ~7 million pump.fun tokens Jan 2024 – Mar 2025: 98.6% flagged as rug pulls or manipulative schemes; fewer than ~100,000 (≈1.4%) ever maintained >$1,000 liquidity. Of 388,000 Raydium liquidity pools examined, 93% showed soft-rug patterns (developer abruptly withdrawing funds). 25% of Raydium rugs involved less than $732; median rug $2,832; largest identified $1.9M (MToken). Pump.fun publicly disputed the methodology (CoinDesk, May 7 2025), arguing that a $1,000-liquidity floor conflates 'failed/abandoned' with 'fraudulent'.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Adopt the $1,000-liquidity floor as a hard universe filter: never trade a pool with < $1,000 (≈5 SOL) of quote-side liquidity — it is definitionally in the 98.6% bucket. Also note the median rug is tiny ($2,832), which means your own position size is often comparable to the entire extractable value; if your intended position is >2-3% of pool depth you are the exit liquidity. Cap position at a fixed fraction of quote reserves (suggest ≤1%).

findings.claim: 92.22% of pump.fun tokens with ≥30 swaps exhibit at least one statistically detected dump event
findings.detail: Marino et al. (arXiv:2602.14860): of 184,282 tokens with ≥30 swaps, 169,938 (92.22%) show at least one dump event under a Shewhart control-chart detector with a k=4 sigma threshold. The distribution of dump counts is right-skewed — most tokens have zero or few, a minority show repeated episodes.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Implement the Shewhart k=4σ control chart on the signed SOL flow / price return series as a real-time exit trigger. Compute a rolling mean and sigma over the last N swaps (N≈30) and exit immediately on a −4σ excursion. This is a published, parameterized detector — use k=4 as the default and tune on your own data. Also use 'number of prior dump events' as a per-token risk feature.

findings.claim: Coordinated bundling is pervasive: 28.13% of holders belong to bundles controlling 36.5% of total supply; high-risk tokens show +24pp top-10 concentration growth and +17pp first-10-buyer share
findings.detail: MemeTrans/MELT (arXiv:2602.13480): bundle-revealed ownership across 41,470 migrated tokens — 28.13% of holders belong to coordinated bundles holding 36.5% of total supply. Decomposition: fund-flow relationships 22.57% of holders / 28.22% of supply; Jito bundle IDs 10.39% of holders / 15.96% of supply; co-purchase 6.46% of holders / 9.16% of supply. High-risk vs low-risk deltas: top-10 holder concentration increase +24pp (vs +6pp for low-risk); first-10-buyers share +17pp; first-20-buyers share +19pp. Also 98.7% of 'create' events co-occur with a developer buy in the same transaction. Separately, arXiv:2607.02795 identified 1,012 persistent sniper wallet cohorts (2,965 addresses, cohort size 2–12, median 2) across 166,098 launches over 13.4 days (Jun 11–25 2026); matched-pair estimate of their causal effect on first-30-min buyer count is only +16.1% (95% CI +13.0%, +19.4%), with SOL-inflow lift +6.3% (CI −0.5%, +15.1%, not significant) — the naive uncontrolled contrast of +130.9% is mostly contamination.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Build three concrete rejection filters with these thresholds: (1) reject if the union of Jito-bundle-cofunded + fund-flow-linked + same-block-co-purchase wallets holds >30% of supply (population mean for the bundled cohort is 36.5%); (2) reject if first-10-buyers collectively hold >~35-40% of supply (high-risk tokens run +17pp above baseline); (3) reject if top-10 non-LP holder concentration is RISING by more than ~15pp between creation and migration. Fund-flow clustering (common funder within N hops) is the single highest-yield detector at 22.57% of holders — implement it first, before Jito bundle ID matching. Do NOT over-weight sniper-cohort presence as a bullish signal: the causal lift on real buyer flow is only ~16%, and half the apparent effect is the snipers counting themselves.

findings.claim: The only published selection strategy with real numbers still LOSES 26.64% on average — nobody has published a profitable memecoin strategy
findings.detail: MemeTrans/MELT (arXiv:2602.13480) 'practical application' experiment on the 21,635-token filtered set (74.18% high-risk, 25.82% normal). Model-guided top-100 selection: 76% precision, 26.64% average loss. Random top-100 baseline: 25.4% precision, 60.71% average loss. Loss reduction 34.07 percentage points. Top-200: model 75.5% precision / 31.47% loss vs random 26.5% / 64.84%. Best single model was an MLP: AUPRC 0.5729, high-risk precision 0.8459, recall 0.8325, F1 0.8391; best ensemble MLP+LSTM AUPRC 0.5827. Time-series-only models underperformed badly (LSTM 0.5023, GRU 0.4972, TCN 0.4844, Transformer 0.4841). 122 features in 5 groups; ablation shows market-activity features (group 3) and bundle statistics (group 4) matter most.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Calibrate expectations hard against this. A state-of-the-art classifier on migration-time features gets you from −61% to −27% average outcome — it is a loss-reduction tool, not an alpha source. Therefore: (a) your P&L must come from exit timing and asymmetric position sizing, not from picking winners; (b) budget for a directional edge that is negative and require the exit policy to make up >27pp; (c) reuse their architecture choice — a plain MLP on tabular features beat every sequence model, so do NOT start with a Transformer; (d) copy the 5-group feature taxonomy, prioritizing market activity + bundle statistics.

findings.claim: Manipulation classifier on price series achieves 87.85% accuracy / 0.9320 AUC using recurring sell-buy cycle structure
findings.detail: MemeTrans (arXiv:2602.13480v1): a Temporal Convolutional Network trained on 1,555 manually-labeled memecoins detects 'recurring, structured sell-buy cycles' indicative of coordinated manipulation, achieving 87.85% accuracy and 0.9320 AUC on held-out test data. Risk labels: high-risk = min_price_ratio < 0.3 OR manipulation score ≥ 0.7; low-risk = min_price_ratio ≥ 0.7 AND manipulation score < 0.3.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Replicate this as a live pre-trade gate: TCN over the OHLCV/trade sequence, reject if manipulation score ≥ 0.7. Their labeling rule (min_price_ratio at 20 min post-migration) is directly reproducible from your own indexer — you can regenerate labels for your own chain/venue without manual annotation for the price half of the rule.

findings.claim: Retail profitability estimates disagree by an order of magnitude — 6.25% vs 73.28% profitable — because of methodology, and the difference is decision-critical
findings.detail: SOURCE A (CoinGecko Research, Dune Solana data, pump.fun wallets, realized PnL netted per wallet across all tokens): monthly % profitable — Apr 2024 47.58%, Nov 2024 38.82%, Feb 2025 35.90%, Jun 2025 30.08% (trough), Nov 2025 44.84%, Jan 2026 50.08%, Feb 2026 56.83%, Mar 2026 70.00%, Apr 2026 73.28%. April 2026: 3,142,559 active wallets; profit $1-500 = 2,047,085 (65.14%); $500-1,000 = 87,127 (2.77%); >$1,000 = 168,795 (5.37%); loss $1-500 = 792,724 (25.23%); loss $500-1,000 = 22,290 (0.71%); loss >$1,000 = 24,538 (0.78%). CoinGecko's own caveats: realized PnL only (excludes wallets holding worthless bags they never sold), bot and wash trading unfiltered, Dune pricing gaps for illiquid tokens. SOURCE B (Dune-based Solana DEX meme traders, 90 days ending ~Aug 19 2026, via Cryptopolitan): 304,161 active traders, 19,003 profitable = 6.25%; 88% of profitable made under $100; only 25 wallets made over $10,000; median trader loss $120; aggregate group loss $1.26B. SOURCE C (crypto.news research, Aug 26 2024, 29,601,462 pump.fun wallets): 37.6% positive PnL (11,126,772), 59.9% negative (17,725,908); >$1,000 profit 0.76%; >$10,000 0.046%; >$100,000 0.0033%; >$1,000,000 0.00054%. SOURCE D (Aug 2024, Dune): 76,567 traders (3.061%) profited >$1,000; ~20% of users profitable.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Treat Source C's tail percentiles as the calibration target because they are internally consistent and the sample is the full wallet population: P(a wallet clears $1,000 lifetime) ≈ 0.76%, P($10,000) ≈ 0.046%, P($100,000) ≈ 0.0033%. Do NOT use CoinGecko's 73% headline as evidence the game got easy — the realized-PnL-only methodology structurally excludes the modal outcome (buy, go to zero, never sell), which is exactly the outcome your bot will experience if it lacks forced exits. Practical consequence: implement forced liquidation on every position so that your own PnL accounting is realized and not flattered.

findings.claim: Profits follow an extreme power law: 12 of ~12.9M pump.fun tokens hold >55% of aggregate FDMC; ~89 of ~2M tokens were above $1M market cap at one point in 2024
findings.detail: Galaxy Research (Oct 1 2025): pump.fun tokens represent $4.8B aggregate FDMC across ~12.9M tokens launched, of which just 12 tokens account for >55% of that FDMC. Solana total token count ~32M (from <8M pre-pump.fun). Decrypt (Sept 12 2024, Dune data): only 89 pump.fun tokens were above $1M market cap = 0.0045% of the ~2M then launched; ~0.3% of GRADUATED tokens maintain a $1M+ market cap; 1.5% of the prior 24h launches graduated. Galaxy also reports Axiom generated >$200M in fees with fewer than 10 employees, and pump.fun ~$120M in fees over 30 days — the reliable money is the toll booth, not the trade.
findings.actionable_for_bot: $1M market cap is ~14.5x from the $69k graduation FDV. The 'maintained $1M+' rate among graduates is ~0.3%, so P(sustained 14.5x from graduation) ≈ 0.3%; the ever-touched rate is higher but I could not verify it — do not assume more than a few percent. Consequence: a hold-for-the-runner strategy is not supportable by these base rates. Structure the bot as a high-frequency, small-multiple, fast-exit system (targeting 1.3x-2x with tight stops) rather than a lottery-ticket system, unless you can independently measure a >2% ever-touched 10x rate on your own data.

findings.claim: Wash trading share estimates differ by two to three orders of magnitude between Solana launchpads and EVM DEXs
findings.detail: MELT (arXiv:2602.13480), pump.fun pre-migration transactions (30.8M total): normal buy/sell 73.5%, WASH TRADES 21.4%, transfers 4.9%. Chainalysis (2024, Ethereum + BNB Chain + Base): Heuristic 1 (buy and sell within 25 blocks ≈ 5 min, volume difference <1%, three or more matching trades by one address) → $704M suspected wash volume = 0.035% of DEX volume; Heuristic 2 (self-funded address clusters) → $1.87B = 0.046%; combined upper bound $2.57B. Chainalysis operator scale: average controller managed 183 addresses (max 22,832), average wash volume per operator $3,661,934 (max $313,585,875). The gap is partly definitional (MELT counts transactions, Chainalysis counts USD volume) and partly real (Solana launchpads are far more manipulated than EVM DEX pairs).
findings.actionable_for_bot: Use MELT's 21.4% as the Solana prior: assume roughly one in five pre-migration trades is fake and discount raw volume/trade-count features by ~20% before feeding them to a model. Implement Chainalysis Heuristic 1 verbatim as a cheap real-time filter — same address, buy and sell within 25 blocks, notional difference <1%, three or more occurrences — and subtract those trades from your volume and unique-trader features. Do not port the EVM 0.04% figure to Solana.

findings.claim: 3.59% of ALL tokens launched in 2024 across chains matched pump-and-dump patterns; 94% of those pools were rugged by the deployer, average 6.23 days to abandonment
findings.detail: Chainalysis 2024: 74,037 suspected pump-and-dump tokens out of 2,063,519 total launched = 3.59%. 42.54% of launched tokens (873,957) ever got listed on a DEX. Only 1.7% of launched tokens were actively traded within the last 30 days. Of suspected pump-and-dump pools, 94% were rugged by the deployer address, with an average duration before abandonment of 6.23 days; 1% of schemes lasted over 4-5 months. Case study: Volume.li bot service generated $257.5M in volume to date, priced at 0.212 ETH per $100,000 of volume (100 buy-sell pairs), and produced 43% of Uniswap trading volume for one token over 4 days.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Two hard filters: (1) deployer-address reputation — 94% of pump-and-dump pools are rugged by the deployer, so maintain a persistent deployer blacklist keyed on the creator wallet and its funding ancestors; a creator with any prior rugged token is a hard reject. (2) age gate — average scheme life is 6.23 days, so a token older than ~7 days that is still trading is in a materially different (safer) population than a fresh launch; consider separate models for <24h and >7d cohorts. Also: the Volume.li price point (0.212 ETH per $100k volume) tells you fake volume costs ~0.6-0.8% of notional — any token whose 'volume' would be cheap to fake at that rate should have volume down-weighted.

findings.claim: Social-channel presence is the strongest cheap pre-trade feature: 8.9x graduation lift for Telegram, 17.4x for all three channels
findings.detail: Kamat (arXiv:2607.02823), 832,941 launches May 8–Jun 10 2026: launches advertising a Telegram channel graduate at 1.485% vs 0.166% without = 8.94x lift; Cox hazard ratio 5.40 (95% CI 4.73–6.17). All three social channels (Telegram + Twitter + website) = 1.919% vs 0.110% for none = 17.4x lift. Individual Cox HRs: Twitter 1.305 (1.192–1.428), website 1.194 (1.096–1.300), log market cap 4.506 (4.293–4.729). Overall Cox concordance 0.858 (bootstrap CI 0.850–0.870). Top market-cap quartile graduation rate 0.634% (0.601–0.669%). Dataset released CC-BY-4.0 on Zenodo, concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.20633486. CAVEAT: the author discloses the collector's effective coverage window was ~6 minutes rather than 24 hours, so all absolute rates are lower bounds; the relative lifts are more robust than the levels. Corroborating from MemeChain (arXiv:2601.22185, 31,811 tokens across 4 chains): Telegram present on 80.85% of projects (91.8% on BSC), X on 68.67%, Discord on 6.69%; of 23,755 tokens claiming a website, only 6,766 (32.09%) returned HTTP 200.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Cheapest high-value filter you can build: parse the token metadata URI at creation for telegram/twitter/website fields. Require at least Telegram (8.9x lift) and preferably all three (17.4x). Then go one step further than the paper: MemeChain shows 67.91% of claimed websites are dead, so actually HTTP-HEAD the URL and require a 200 — the ~32% that resolve are a much stronger cohort than the 74.8% that merely claim one. Note this feature is trivially gameable and its predictive power will decay; re-fit monthly. Also note log market cap has the highest Cox HR (4.5) — curve progress dominates everything else.

findings.claim: Round-trip trading friction on Solana memecoins is 2.5% to 6% before slippage, and unprotected swaps lose ~3% to sandwich MEV
findings.detail: Pump.fun bonding curve: 1.25% total per trade = 0.95% protocol + 0.30% creator (Marino et al. confirm the same split). PumpSwap canonical pools: fee declines with SOL-denominated market cap, from 1.25% total at 0–420 SOL mcap down to 0.30% total at ≥98,240 SOL; non-canonical pools flat 0.30%. PumpSwap originally launched at 0.25% (≈0.20% LP + 0.05% protocol). Token creation costs 0 SOL plus network fee; a 0.015 SOL graduation fee is referenced. MEV: Helius reports a single sandwich bot ('Vpe') executed 1.55M transactions over 30 days at 88.9% success, extracting 65,880 SOL ($13.43M) at an average 0.0425 SOL ($8.67) profit per attack, paying 22,760 SOL in Jito tips; 16 of its top 20 victim tokens were pump.fun tokens. Over 500K sandwich instances and >$7.7M victim losses in ~4 months of early-2025 Jito data; $370M–$500M extracted Jan 2024–May 2025. Practitioner estimate: a 1 SOL (~$200) unprotected memecoin swap on Raydium loses ~3% to fees and bots vs ~0.7% with MEV protection. Solana base fee 5,000 lamports/signature plus priority fee.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Budget c = 5% round-trip friction as the default in all EV math (1.25% in + 1.25% out on curve, plus ~1-2% net slippage/MEV, plus priority fees and Jito tips). Route every swap through an MEV-protected path (Jito bundle or a private relay) — the measured delta is ~3% → ~0.7%, i.e. ~2.3pp of round-trip edge recovered, which is larger than most model improvements you will achieve. Never set a wide slippage tolerance: Helius/Chainalysis both attribute memecoin sandwich vulnerability to high slippage settings on illiquid pools. Cap slippage at 3-5% and prefer failing the trade.

findings.claim: Break-even hit rates at realistic friction: 52.5% for a 2x target, 21.0% for 5x, 10.5% for 10x, 2.1% for 50x, 1.05% for 100x (full loss on losers)
findings.detail: Derived, not from a source. With equal position sizing, expected net return = p(M−1) − (1−p)L − c, so break-even p = (L + c) / (M − 1 + L), where M = win multiple, L = fractional loss on losers, c = round-trip friction. At c = 0.05: M=2 → p=52.5% (L=1.0) or 44.1% (L=0.7); M=5 → 21.0% (L=1.0) or 16.0% (L=0.7); M=10 → 10.5% (L=1.0) or 8.7% (L=0.8); M=50 → 2.1%; M=100 → 1.05%. Compare to measured base rates: only 5.20% of migrated tokens never dip below entry at all (MELT), the graduate rate (≈15x from launch) is 0.2–1.8% in normal regimes, and only ~0.3% of graduates sustain $1M (≈14.5x from graduation).
findings.actionable_for_bot: Hardcode this break-even function and evaluate every candidate strategy against it before writing execution code. The comparison that matters: a 10x-target strategy needs a 10.5% hit rate, but the measured population rate of a ~15x from launch is ~1% — so a viable 10x strategy needs its selection model to deliver a >10x lift over base rate, which is roughly the magnitude of the social-presence lift (8.9x-17.4x) and nothing else in the literature. A 2x-target strategy needs 52.5%, versus a 5.20% population rate of not even dipping — that requires an even bigger relative lift and is likely unreachable without stops. Conclusion to encode: run tight stops so L falls to ~0.3, which drops the 5x break-even to (0.30+0.05)/4.30 = 8.1% and the 2x break-even to (0.30+0.05)/1.30 = 26.9%. Stop-loss discipline moves the break-even more than any model will.

findings.claim: Cross-chain: BSC/four.meme has a comparable ~1.34% graduation rate and much higher token mortality than Solana
findings.detail: four.meme (BNB Chain), reported figures: ~384,000 tokens created, ~5,150 graduated ≈ 1.34% graduation rate, ~26,300+ BNB in fees — I could not locate a primary source for these, treat as unverified. MemeChain (arXiv:2601.22185), 31,811 validated tokens (BSC 15,455 / Solana 11,809 / Ethereum 3,720 / Base 827), collected mid-Oct 2024 and tracked to mid-Jan 2025: 'one-day' coins (ceased trading within 24h) — BSC 10.35%, Base 7.62%, Ethereum 3.47%, Solana 0.09%; inactive after Dec 15 2024 — BSC 80.96%, Ethereum 37.32%, Base 16.20%, Solana 9.09%. Overall 47.46% inactive; 15.53% lasted ≤30 days; 11.04% ≤7 days. Base Clanker: >167,000 tokens launched, >10,000/day during Mar 11-15 peak; at least three exceeded $10M market cap (LUM $33M, ANON $46M, CLANKER $70M).
findings.actionable_for_bot: The MemeChain per-chain mortality numbers are from a curated (not exhaustive) sample and its Solana subset is clearly survivorship-selected — the 0.09% one-day rate contradicts CoinGecko's 68.67% on the full pump.fun population, so do NOT use MemeChain for absolute Solana base rates. What is usable: BSC token mortality is materially worse than Base or Ethereum in the same sample (80.96% vs 16.20% vs 37.32% inactive), so if you extend to a second chain, prefer Base over BSC on survival grounds. Re-derive four.meme and Clanker graduation rates from your own indexer before allocating capital there — no reliable published figure exists.

findings.claim: Bot infrastructure benchmarks: on-chain bot clusters show 91.8%-99.5% transaction success rates for viable operations vs <10.5% for failing ones
findings.detail: arXiv:2607.28424 ('Demystifying Solana Bots'), 586 GitHub bot repos + 200 bot-associated on-chain addresses + 44,118,825 transactions, baseline Oct 1–Nov 1 2025, validated Feb 1–Mar 1 2026. Four clusters: Cluster 2 (aggregator-centric MEV) median success 0.975 / mean 0.918, 0.457 tx/sec, 62.3% of transactions profitable when routing via HumidiFi vs 21.01% otherwise; Cluster 3 (trading operations) median success 0.999 / mean 0.995, 9.82e-4 tx/sec, 80.9% of transactions on pump.fun, 43.14% of addresses at 100% success; Cluster 1 (venue-specialized MEV) median 0.020 / mean 0.105, 1.360 tx/sec, 72.73% of addresses below 0.2 success; Cluster 0 (multi-venue MEV) median 0.017 / mean 0.073, 84.85% below 0.2 success. Repo category counts: order execution 137, sniping 134, arbitrage 47, tx-ordering exploitation 41, copy trading 33, wash trading 21. Bot-attributed DEX trading exceeded $250M/day as of Jan 2026. WSOL is the pivot token in 99.94%/98.25% of Cluster 1/2 transactions but only 10.93% of Cluster 3.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Use transaction success rate as your primary operational health metric with a hard alarm: if your landed-transaction rate falls below ~90% you are in the failing-bot regime (Clusters 0/1 sit under 10.5%) and burning fees for nothing. A directional trading bot (Cluster 3 profile) should target >99% landed rate and LOW submission frequency (they run ~1 tx per 17 minutes per address) — high tx/sec is the MEV-searcher profile, not the memecoin-trading profile. Also note Cluster 3 concentrates 80.9% of activity on pump.fun and mostly does not pivot through WSOL — match that pattern to avoid being fingerprinted as an MEV bot.

findings.claim: Copy-trading a curated KOL wallet set produced ~$500,000 across 1,000 projects with ~70-73% agent precision — the closest thing to a published live-strategy result
findings.detail: arXiv:2601.08641 ('Resisting Manipulative Bots in Meme Coin Copy Trading'). Evaluation set: the first 1,000 memecoins migrating after the $TRUMP launch (Jan 17 2025, 14:01:48), tracked from launch through 12 hours post-migration, trading data from Flipside's Solana archive; ~4,000 projects used for model training. Meme-evaluation agent precision 73% at the 30-minute interval (F1 0.7213); best F1 0.6197 at the 1-hour post-migration interval; wallet-evaluation agent precision ~70% (4,773 true positives of 6,879 predictions). Reported profit of the selected KOL wallets: '$500,000 across these projects'. Wash-trading score threshold c = 50 (ratio of matched buy-sell pairs to net position); bundle-bot detection = transactions in the same block as launch plus creator-to-trader fund transfers.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Treat the $500,000 as the aggregate profit of the identified KOL wallets, NOT as a backtested return of a reproducible strategy — no capital base, no drawdown, no fee accounting is given, and the sample is the single most anomalous window in memecoin history ($TRUMP launch). Two things ARE directly reusable: the wash-trading score with threshold c=50 (matched buy-sell pairs / net position) and the bundle-bot definition (same-block-as-launch transactions plus creator→trader fund transfers). Implement both as wallet-quality filters before copying any wallet.

findings.claim: Memecoins as an asset class delivered −78.74% over Jan 2025–Feb 2026 with 103.82% annualized volatility
findings.detail: David Krause, 'An Empirical Analysis of Meme Coin Performance: 2025–2026', SSRN abstract 6292920, published Feb 23 2026. Ten largest meme coins, weekly returns from Yahoo Finance, equally weighted portfolio: −78.74% over the sample vs −30.68% Bitcoin, +17.84% S&P 500, +92.46% gold. Annualized volatility 103.82%; maximum drawdown 82.71%. Best individual coin Dogecoin −70.02%, worst Brett −93.30%. Correlation with Bitcoin 0.78, with gold −0.41. NOTE: this covers large-cap listed memecoins, not launchpad microcaps, and Yahoo Finance weekly data is a weak source for this asset class.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Establishes the beta you are fighting: the memecoin complex itself lost ~79% over 14 months with 0.78 correlation to BTC. Two implications: (1) any long-only memecoin bot inherits a large negative drift — you must be flat or hedged by default and only long when a signal fires; (2) with 0.78 BTC correlation at the large-cap end, use a BTC/SOL regime filter as a global risk switch (halt new entries when SOL is in a defined drawdown), rather than assuming memecoin returns are idiosyncratic.

findings.claim: Pump.fun's share of the Solana token universe and DEX flow is large enough that pump.fun IS the memecoin market
findings.detail: arXiv:2512.11850 (Q4 2024, Dune data): pump.fun accounted for up to 71.1% of all tokens minted on Solana; pump.fun-created tokens generated 40%–67.4% of daily DEX transactions; pump.fun itself was 15-25% of DEX activity; 2-4M pump.fun transactions/day; peak 69,046 tokens minted in one day; daily unique trading addresses peaked at 260,000 (Nov 2024) from ~60,000 (early Oct 2024), 224,000 in Dec 2024. Galaxy (Oct 2025): Solana at ~32M tokens total, ~12.9M from pump.fun. CoinMarketCap Academy (2026): pump.fun holds ~95% of daily token graduation market share after competition from LetsBonk/Believe/Moonshot receded. Marino et al. (Sept-Oct 2025): 2-5M trades/day, peak daily USD volume $600-700M, 2,600,790 distinct traders in one month, 243,123 distinct creators, top creator launched 107 tokens with an 8.4% graduation ratio.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Build the Solana leg against pump.fun/PumpSwap first and treat other launchpads as optional adapters — ~95% of graduations flow through one venue, so a single well-instrumented integration captures nearly the whole opportunity set. The 8.4% graduation rate of the top serial creator (107 tokens) vs the ~0.6-1.8% population rate is a ~5-14x lift: maintain a creator-address leaderboard keyed on historical graduation ratio and require a minimum launch count (e.g. ≥10 prior tokens) before trusting it.
