traps_and_failure_modes: NO published peak-multiple distribution exists. I could not find a single credible source giving the % of memecoins that ever do 2x/5x/10x/50x/100x from launch. Anything you see quoting such a table is almost certainly fabricated or extrapolated. You must generate this yourself from an indexed archive — it is the highest-value missing input to your economics, and it is a one-week data job.

Survivorship bias in every public dataset. MemeChain reports 0.09% one-day mortality for Solana while CoinGecko reports 68.67% on the full population — a 700x discrepancy driven entirely by sample selection. MELT/MemeTrans only contains tokens that MIGRATED (the top ~1%), so its statistics are conditional on graduation and say nothing about the other 99%. Never mix conditional and unconditional base rates in the same EV calculation.

Realized-PnL-only accounting flatters profitability enormously. CoinGecko's 73.28%-profitable April 2026 figure explicitly excludes wallets that bought and never sold — i.e. the modal memecoin outcome. This is why the same period's alternative studies show 6.25%. Your own backtest must mark unsold positions to zero, not exclude them.

The graduation rate is not stationary and mechanics changes invalidate models overnight. It went from ~0.84% in June 2026 to 6.7% in late July 2026 purely because pump.fun shipped BOOST (redeploying ~20% of migration liquidity into post-migration market buys followed by burns). Every model fit before a mechanics change is stale. Subscribe to launchpad changelogs as a first-class data feed.

arXiv:2607.02823's headline 0.198% graduation rate is NOT comparable to Marino's 0.63%. The author discloses the collector's effective coverage window was ~6 minutes, not the claimed 24 hours, making all its absolute rates lower bounds. Its relative effects (social-channel lifts, Cox HRs) are more trustworthy than its levels. The paper's structure (versioned corrigenda, single author, rapid turnaround) also warrants independent replication before you rely on it.

Sniper-cohort presence is a weak signal that looks strong. The naive uncontrolled association between coordinated wallets and first-hour buyer flow is +130.9%; after excluding the cohort's own buys it drops to +63.9%; after propensity matching on launch quality it is +16.1% on buyer count and statistically indistinguishable from zero (+6.3%, CI −0.5% to +15.1%) on SOL inflow. If you naively feed 'snipers present' into a model you will fit contamination, not signal.

The best-published selection model still loses 26.64%. Do not plan a business around a directional edge from a classifier. The MELT top-100 result (76% precision, −26.64%) versus random (25.4%, −60.71%) is the honest ceiling of migration-time feature engineering as of the current literature.

Wide slippage tolerance is how memecoin traders get sandwiched. Both Chainalysis and Helius attribute memecoin sandwich vulnerability specifically to traders setting high slippage on illiquid pools. A single sandwich bot netted $13.43M in 30 days with 16 of its top-20 victim tokens being pump.fun tokens. Route privately and cap slippage.

Your own position can be larger than the entire extractable value. The median Raydium soft rug is $2,832 and 25% are under $732. In pools that thin, backtested fills are fiction. Simulate execution against actual reserve depth, not against a mid price.

Fake volume is cheap. Volume.li charges 0.212 ETH per $100,000 of generated volume (~0.6-0.8% of notional) and produced 43% of one token's Uniswap volume over 4 days. Any strategy keyed on volume or trade count is trivially and cheaply gamed against you.

Wash-trading estimates differ by 500x between sources (21.4% of pump.fun transactions per MELT vs 0.035-0.046% of EVM DEX volume per Chainalysis). This is partly transactions-vs-USD-volume and partly a genuine chain difference. Do not port EVM manipulation priors to Solana launchpads.

Social-presence features are the highest-lift cheap signal AND the most trivially gameable. An 8.94x Telegram lift will be arbitraged away as soon as it is widely known (and it is now published). Re-fit monthly and add liveness/quality checks (HTTP 200, channel member count, account age) rather than mere presence.

Nearly every headline percentage circulating in crypto media traces back to a handful of Dune queries whose SQL you cannot inspect. The '25 wallets made over $10,000' figure in particular is inconsistent with every other source and should not be used. Prefer sources that publish methodology (Chainalysis, CoinGecko, the arXiv papers) over aggregator sites (coinlaw.io and similar returned 403 and could not be verified at all).

Fee schedules changed repeatedly in 2025-2026 (PumpSwap launched at 0.25%, now runs a market-cap-scaled 1.25%→0.30%; creator fee sharing was overhauled Jan 9 2026). Fetch the live fee parameters from chain state rather than hardcoding, or your EV math silently drifts.

Sniper bot & execution platform landscap.topic: Sniper bot & execution platform landscape for Solana memecoins — platform-by-platform teardown and the self-hosted sub-second stack
Sniper bot & execution platform landscap.executive_summary: The single most important finding: BullX/BullX Neo suspended all trading functionality on 1 June 2026 and has not resumed; wallets/withdrawals remain open but the community treats it as a permanent shutdown. Do not architect around it. Second: essentially NONE of the retail "sniper platforms" (Photon, Axiom, Trojan, Bloom, Nova, Vector, Padre/Terminal, Pepeboost, BonkBot, Banana Gun, Maestro) expose a public programmatic trading API — they are UI or Telegram surfaces, and Photon explicitly states it is built for manual trading with third-party automation scripts to be treated as unsafe. The one real exception is GMGN.ai, which publishes a genuine REST trading API (get_swap_route → sign locally → send_transaction), but it is gated behind a volume-based application and rate-limited to one call per five seconds, which disqualifies it as a sniper execution path (it is usable as a fallback/exit router only). Therefore, for a bot that must fire in <1s of a signal, the platform layer is a dead end and the answer is a fully self-hosted stack. Fee-wise the platforms cluster tightly at 1.0% gross with referral/cashback pulling effective rates to roughly 0.75–0.90% (Axiom's published cashback ladder runs Wood 0.95% → Champion 0.75%, with a 10% referral discount; volume thresholds are unpublished), so there is no meaningful fee arbitrage between them — self-hosting saves the entire ~1% platform take, which is the largest single controllable line item. On trust: Axiom suffered a ZachXBT-documented February 2026 insider scandal in which employees used an over-permissive internal admin dashboard to inspect prominent traders' "private-only" wallet activity — for a systematic bot this is strategy-leakage risk, not just reputational. Banana Gun was drained ~$3M across 11 wallets in September 2024 via a Telegram message-oracle bug (fully reimbursed, then hardened with 2FA and a 2-hour transfer delay); Maestro is outright custodial with a single one-time mnemonic export. The recommended best-in-class stack is: Yellowstone gRPC/Geyser (or ShredStream) for detection, locally-constructed pump.fun/PumpSwap/Raydium instructions with no RPC round-trip in the hot path, and submission via Helius Sender Max (0.001 SOL min tip, multi-path to Helius+Jito+Harmonic+Rakurai) and/or direct Jito sendBundle. All-in cost for a self-hosted 1 SOL pump.fun bonding-curve snipe is roughly 1.25% venue fee + ~0.0012 SOL fixed (tip + priority + base) ≈ 1.37% one-way before slippage, versus ~2.37% one-way through a 1% platform. Because tip and priority fees are fixed in SOL and not proportional, there is a hard minimum viable trade size around 0.5 SOL below which fixed costs exceed 0.25% of notional. Critically, Alpenglow's 150ms finality is NOT live — it is targeted for Agave 4.3 / October 2026 mainnet activation, and at least one vendor blog wrongly describes it as already shipped; build against the current 400ms slot. Finally, the base-rate math is brutal and should dominate position sizing: a peer-reviewed survival analysis of 832,941 launches (May–June 2026) puts the pump.fun graduation rate at 0.198%, with presence of a Telegram link lifting it 8.94x and initial market cap above the 30 SOL default being the strongest single predictor (Cox HR 4.51).
Sniper bot & execution platform landscap.executive_summary_note: See findings for per-platform detail, concrete_apis for endpoints, numeric_parameters for hardcodable defaults, and traps_and_failure_modes for the things that will actually kill the bot.

findings.claim: BullX / BullX Neo suspended all trading functionality on 1 June 2026 and has not resumed operations
findings.detail: Trading functionality was suspended starting June 1, 2026, announced via Discord and framed as a pause for 'future upgrades' with no timeline or roadmap published since. Wallet functionality including withdrawals and management remains operational; user assets are not locked. Community consensus treats it as permanent closure. Major grievance: the platform collected a reported >$200M in fees from a userbase that farmed points for an airdrop that never materialized. Prior to shutdown BullX charged 1% and covered ~9 chains. No exploit or breach is associated with the shutdown; trades were executed on-chain with BullX acting as an execution layer rather than a custodian, with private keys reportedly downloadable within 48 hours of wallet creation (that 48h claim is low-confidence secondary sourcing).
findings.actionable_for_bot: Remove BullX/BullX Neo from all integration plans and from any comparison logic. If any legacy code or config references neo.bullx.io, delete it. Treat this as the canonical worked example of platform-dependency risk: any architecture whose execution path routes through a single third-party frontend can be zeroed overnight with no warning, which is the core argument for the self-hosted path.

findings.claim: Axiom is non-custodial via Turnkey, charges 1% gross with a published cashback ladder to 0.75%, but suffered a documented insider-surveillance scandal in February 2026
findings.detail: Fees: 1% gross on spot. Referral signup gives a 10% discount on trading fees (≈0.9% effective from day one); how referral stacks with cashback is undocumented. Cashback ladder (7 tiers, net fee): Wood 0.95%, Bronze 0.90%, Silver 0.875%, Gold 0.85%, Platinum 0.825%, Diamond 0.80%, Champion 0.75%. Volume thresholds per tier are NOT published by Axiom — the source explicitly warns 'Any guide quoting a specific dollar threshold per tier is guessing.' Referral revenue share: 30% direct, 3% second level, 2% third. Perps route to Hyperliquid at 0.01% per transaction plus Hyperliquid's own maker/taker schedule. Default priority fee and Jito tip are both 0.001 SOL, and neither prevents sandwich attacks. Custody: non-custodial, keys managed via Turnkey air-gapped infrastructure; email/Google signup auto-provisions a Turnkey-backed wallet. SECURITY: On 26 February 2026 ZachXBT published an investigation alleging multiple Axiom employees abused internal admin tooling to look up private wallet information and track 'private-only' wallet activity of prominent traders and influencers, beginning early 2025; one employee was named (Broox Bauer). Axiom issued a formal apology, suspended the employees involved, admitted internal access controls were 'unnecessarily permissive', and promised an internal audit. Axiom is a Y Combinator W25 company.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Do not route bot flow through Axiom. The insider incident is not a fund-loss risk (non-custodial) but is a strategy-leakage risk: an operator with dashboard access could observe your wallet's entry patterns and front-run or copy them, which directly degrades alpha for a systematic strategy. If you use Axiom at all, use it only as a manual research UI with a wallet that never touches bot capital, and never label wallets in-app. Also note the 0.001 SOL default Jito tip as a useful reference point — it matches Helius Sender Max's minimum and is a sane hardcoded default for your own tip floor.

findings.claim: GMGN.ai is the only major platform in this set exposing a genuine public trading API, but its 1-call-per-5-seconds rate limit disqualifies it for sniping
findings.detail: Three endpoints. (1) Route: GET https://gmgn.ai/defi/router/v1/sol/tx/get_swap_route with params token_in_address, token_out_address, in_amount (lamports), from_address, slippage. Returns quote plus an unsigned base64 transaction. Anti-MEV via Jito supported with is_anti_mev=true and a minimum 0.002 SOL fee. (2) Submit: POST https://gmgn.ai/txproxy/v1/send_transaction — you base64-decode the returned tx, deserialize as VersionedTransaction, sign with your local key, re-encode base64, post. (3) Status: GET https://gmgn.ai/defi/router/v1/sol/tx/get_transaction_status with hash and last_valid_height; transactions expire after ~60 seconds. Auth: apply via Google Form, approval granted solely on sufficient GMGN trading volume, reviewed within 24h, API key emailed and passed in the x-route-key header. RATE LIMIT: 'Each API Key is rate-limited to one call every 5 seconds.' Custody is effectively non-custodial for API use since you sign locally. Platform fee ~1% (0.9–1% with referral discounts). GMGN also ships an Agent API / MCP skill架 at github.com/GMGNAI/gmgn-skills covering Solana, BSC and Base. Reputation: widely regarded as best-in-class for copy trading and wallet analytics, but reported to lag during extreme volume spikes.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Do NOT put GMGN in the hot path — one call per 5 seconds means you cannot even fetch a route within your <1s budget for more than one signal per 5s, and the route call is a network round-trip on top. Two legitimate uses: (a) a non-latency-critical exit/unwind router when you want their multi-DEX routing and don't care about 300ms, and (b) their analytics endpoints for offline smart-money wallet discovery to seed your copy-trade signal list. Budget the 0.002 SOL minimum if you set is_anti_mev=true. Note the ~60s last_valid_height expiry as a general Solana blockhash-lifetime constraint that applies to your self-built transactions too.

findings.claim: Photon (photon-sol.tinyastro.io) charges a flat 1% with no tiers or referral discount and explicitly has no automation API
findings.detail: 1% fee on every trade, buy or sell, on top of Solana network fees and any priority fee you set. No published volume tiers and no published referral discount — the only major platform in this set with neither. Runs at photon-sol.tinyastro.io and nowhere else (phishing clones are common). Custody: non-custodial in structure, but the private key export is ONE-TIME from the Settings menu, which is a meaningful operational risk — if you miss it you cannot re-export. API: 'Photon is built for manual trading and does not provide an official API for automation or bot trading. Any third-party scripts claiming Photon automation should be considered unsafe.' No security incident found for Photon in this research. Positioned as the oldest Solana web trader; competitors characterize it as showing its age, notably charging full 1% with zero rebate while rivals return 10–45%.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Exclude entirely from the bot architecture — there is no supported programmatic surface, and any scraped/reverse-engineered driver is both fragile and an explicit ToS/safety violation. If a human operator uses Photon for discovery, export the private key immediately on wallet creation (one-time only) and treat that wallet as compromised-by-default for bot purposes. Photon is the worst fee deal in the set at a true 1.00% effective with no rebate path.

findings.claim: Telegram bots (Trojan, BonkBot, Banana Gun, Maestro, Bloom, Nova, Pepeboost) all cluster at 1% with varying rebates, and differ mainly on custody model and incident history — none offers a public API
findings.detail: Trojan: 1% base, 10% fee discount via referral, Arena cashback up to 45% giving ~0.55% effective (one source); another source puts referral tier 3 at 0.5% and base-with-referral at 0.75–1%. Telegram-native with no web interface. Bot generates and manages the wallet; private key is exportable and Trojan supports MULTIPLE key exports. Claimed $21.4B+ lifetime volume, 1M+ users. Effectively custodial until you export and sweep — should hold a disposable float, not a bankroll. BonkBot: 1%. Non-custodial KMS third-party audited by OtterSec; 2FA required for SOL withdrawals and private-key exports; multiple key exports supported. Best security posture in the Telegram cohort. Banana Gun: 1% on snipes, 0.5% on other trades. Ships a 'Banana Simulator' honeypot pre-check. ONE-TIME key export only. INCIDENT: September 2024, a Telegram message oracle vulnerability let attackers manually initiate transfers from 11 actively-trading users' wallets, draining ~$3M (initially reported ~$1.9M); both EVM and Solana bots affected despite independent codebases; the manual (not automated) nature indicated targeting of 'smart money'. Both bots shut down immediately, vulnerability patched, all victims fully reimbursed from treasury with no token sales, then a 2-hour transfer delay and 2FA on transfers added plus Security Alliance (SEAL) external pentest. Maestro: 1% on successful buys, sells and presale snipes (transfers untaxed); Premium plan ~$200/month for faster execution, up to 10 wallets, priority copy trading; /cashback gives volume-based rebate up to 30%. CUSTODIAL — private key is generated and held on Maestro infrastructure so the bot can sign instantly; only a SINGLE mnemonic export is permitted. Supports SOL, ETH, BSC, BASE, MONAD, SONIC, AVAX, ARB, HYPE, TRX, TON at 1% across all chains. Historic ~$200k loss in the same 2023 exploit wave that hit Unibot. Bloom: 1% (0.9% with referral), non-custodial with AES-encrypted wallets, covers Raydium/Pump.fun/Orca/Meteora. Nova: 1% plus gas and MEV tip, up to 10 wallets, explicitly still 'Phase 1' with a short track record. Pepeboost: 1%, 0.9% with referral, Turbo Mode and anti-MEV. Padre (rebranded Terminal): 0.5–1% base with 10–20% cashback for ~0.8% effective per one source, 35% cashback per another — sources disagree. MEVx: 0.8% flat across 6 chains per one source, 0.9–1% per another — sources disagree. Vector: no substantive fee, custody or API data located in this research.
findings.actionable_for_bot: None of these are drivable programmatically in a supported way — Telegram userbot automation is against Telegram ToS, brittle against UI changes, and adds 100s of ms of messaging latency on top of execution, so it cannot meet a <1s budget. Use this table only for (a) benchmarking what fee your self-hosted bot must beat (≈0.75–1.00% saved per side) and (b) custody triage if a human operator runs a manual sleeve. Custody ranking for any manual sleeve: BonkBot (audited non-custodial KMS + 2FA + multi-export) > Trojan/Bloom (non-custodial-ish, multi-export) > Banana Gun (one-time export, but strong post-incident hardening and a perfect reimbursement record) > Maestro (custodial, single export — avoid). Vector should be marked unverified rather than assumed 1%.

findings.claim: Jito is the atomic-bundle layer: max 5 transactions, 1,000 lamport minimum tip, 1 request/second/IP/region default rate limit
findings.detail: Mainnet block engine: https://mainnet.block-engine.jito.wtf. Regional endpoints in Amsterdam, Dublin, Frankfurt, London, New York, Salt Lake City, Singapore, Tokyo. Testnet at https://testnet.block-engine.jito.wtf (Dallas, New York). Bundles: maximum 5 transactions, executed sequentially and atomically (all-or-nothing). Minimum tip 1,000 lamports (0.000001 SOL). Rate limit: 'one request per second per IP per region', 429 on exceed, custom limits via Discord ticket. Tip floor REST API: https://bundles.jito.wtf/api/v1/bundles/tip_floor, plus a tip_stream WebSocket for live percentile pricing. sendTransaction acts as a proxy to Solana's native method with MEV protection by default, recommended fee split 70% priority fee / 30% Jito tip, and bundleOnly=true for revert protection. sendBundle ignores priority fee entirely — only the tip matters — and requires the tip instruction inside the bundle. ShredStream is offered for sub-slot block data delivery. NOTE: one secondary source claimed 'Jito no longer provides a minimum tip'; the official Jito docs state 1,000 lamports, so trust the docs.
findings.actionable_for_bot: The 1 req/s/IP/region limit is the binding constraint most teams miss — a single IP cannot submit more than one bundle per second per region. Mitigate by submitting the same bundle to multiple regional endpoints concurrently (each has its own budget) and/or by requesting a raised limit. Use sendBundle when you need atomicity (e.g. buy + a conditional guard tx, or a buy that must revert together with a check); use sendTransaction with bundleOnly=true when you just want revert protection on a single swap. Poll the tip_floor REST endpoint or subscribe to tip_stream on a background timer (every 5–10s) and cache the percentiles — never fetch tip data inside the hot path.

findings.claim: LIVE Jito tip-floor data fetched 2026-08-23 shows landed tips far below the 0.001 SOL minimums that sender services impose
findings.detail: Fetched directly from https://bundles.jito.wtf/api/v1/bundles/tip_floor on 2026-08-23: 25th percentile 1.7055e-6 SOL; 50th percentile 5e-6 SOL; 75th percentile 7.128e-6 SOL; 95th percentile 9.2676e-5 SOL; 99th percentile 7.022605e-4 SOL. The 99th percentile (0.000702 SOL) is still BELOW the 0.001 SOL minimum tip required by Helius Sender Max and Nozomi. Separately, practitioner guidance holds that the tip ceiling for genuinely competitive opportunities has stabilized at roughly 50–70% of expected profit, and recommends paying the 75th percentile for a normal launch and the 95th when the block is contested; one vendor's dynamic engine samples the last 50 successful inclusions for the opportunity category and bids the 80th percentile.
findings.actionable_for_bot: This is the key cost insight: for ordinary (non-contested) transactions the landed tip market is cheap — a 0.000005 SOL median tip lands the median bundle. But the moment you use Helius Sender Max or Nozomi you are forced to 0.001 SOL, which is ~200x the median and ~1.4x the 99th percentile. So route selection is a real cost decision, not a formality: use the cheap SWQOS-only path (0.000005 SOL min) for non-contested exits and scale-outs, and reserve the 0.001 SOL Sender Max / Jito path for contested entries. Implement tip as max(p75_from_tip_floor, service_minimum) for normal fires and max(p95, service_minimum) for contested ones, with an absolute cap at 50–70% of modeled expected profit so a fat-finger signal cannot tip away the entire edge. Refresh percentiles on a 5–10s background poll.

findings.claim: Helius Sender is the strongest single submission primitive for a sub-second bot: multi-path routing, regional HTTP endpoints, 50 TPS, and no API credit consumption
findings.detail: Frontend HTTPS: https://sender.helius-rpc.com/fast (auto-routes globally) and https://sender.helius-rpc.com/ping (connection warming). Regional backend HTTP endpoints: http://slc-sender.helius-rpc.com/fast (Salt Lake City), ewr- (Newark), lon- (London), fra- (Frankfurt), ams- (Amsterdam), sg- (Singapore), tyo- (Tokyo). Two tiers: Sender Max requires a 0.001 SOL minimum tip and routes across ALL high-speed pathways simultaneously (Helius, Jito, Harmonic, Rakurai) with a priority tip buffer for top-of-block; SWQOS-only requires just 0.000005 SOL minimum tip, uses a single SWQOS path, and is selected by appending ?swqos_only=true. EVERY transaction must include BOTH a SOL tip transfer to a designated tip account AND a compute unit price instruction via ComputeBudgetProgram.setComputeUnitPrice — omitting either is rejected. Rate limit 50 transactions/second by default, consuming no API credits, with custom limits for Professional plan users. Options: skipPreflight:true lowers latency by skipping validation; ?mev-protect=true routes around validators linked to sandwich attacks. Competing services: Nozomi/Temporal (from Harmonic's team, self-hosted nodes + staked connections + Jito bundles, API key passed as a query parameter /?c=<YOUR_API_KEY>, requires base64 encoding rather than Solana's default base58, minimum tip reported at 0.001 SOL); 0slot.trade with regions in New York, Frankfurt, Amsterdam, Tokyo and Los Angeles; Astralane; Sanctum Gateway.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Make Helius Sender the primary submission path. Concrete implementation: (1) pin to the regional endpoint nearest your compute (co-locate in Newark or Frankfurt near validator concentration); (2) run a keepalive hitting /ping every few seconds so the TCP/TLS connection is warm and idle latency does not spike — this is free latency and almost everyone forgets it; (3) always set skipPreflight:true in the hot path since preflight is a full extra RPC simulation round-trip; (4) always attach both the tip transfer and setComputeUnitPrice or the submission is rejected; (5) implement the SWQOS-only vs Max tier as a runtime switch keyed off contested-ness, since the tip minimums differ by 200x. Note the regional endpoints are plain HTTP not HTTPS — that is deliberate (TLS handshake elimination) but means you must not send anything secret over them beyond the signed transaction, which is fine since signed txs are public anyway. Fan out to Jito sendBundle in parallel for redundancy; duplicate landings are prevented by Solana's transaction dedup, so parallel submission is free insurance.

findings.claim: Jupiter Ultra is well-engineered but structurally too slow for a <1s sniper — its own published latencies exceed the budget
findings.detail: Published endpoint latencies: /order 300ms P50; /execute 700ms to 2s roundtrip; /holdings 70ms; /shield 150ms; /search 15ms. 95% of swaps execute within 2 seconds via Jupiter Beam. Fee: 5–10 basis points (0.05–0.10%) in swap fees; integrators can layer custom fees on top. Features a Real-Time Slippage Estimator (RTSE) using token categories, historical data, exponential moving averages and real-time failure monitoring; Jupiter Beam provides transaction privacy until on-chain execution to reduce front-running by avoiding public mempool exposure; gasless support when users lack SOL, plus market-maker-funded transactions via JupiterZ (RFQ). Rate limits: base 50 requests per 10-second sliding window, with added quota scaling on 24h swap volume — $0 volume → +0 (50 total), $10,000 → +1 (51), $100,000 → +11 (61), $1,000,000 → +115 (165 total); quota recalculates every 10 minutes on a rolling 24h basis; free API key, no paid tiers for Ultra, and the formula is explicitly 'subject to changes'. Separately the general Jupiter platform has a free Lite tier at lite-api.jup.ag (60-second rate window) and paid Pro tiers at pro-api.jup.ag (10-second windows; Pro II = 500 req/10s default bucket + 500 req/10s price bucket). Legacy portal users kept old rate limits free only until 30 June 2026 — that deadline has passed. Metis/Swap V2 is the alternative for CPI capabilities, custom instructions and full transaction control, and supports integrator fees via the platformFeeBps parameter on /quote; since January 2025 you no longer need the Referral Program and can pass any valid token account as feeAccount.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Do not use Ultra for entries. /order at 300ms P50 plus /execute at 700ms–2s means the aggregator alone can consume your entire budget before a transaction is even broadcast. Use Jupiter in two non-hot-path roles instead: (a) Swap V2/Metis to BUILD instructions for multi-hop or illiquid exits where routing quality beats latency, taking the transaction and submitting it yourself through Helius Sender rather than through Jupiter's /execute; (b) the /shield endpoint (150ms) as an offline or pre-trade token-safety signal. Also verify your billing is set up on the new Developer Platform since the free legacy grandfathering expired 30 June 2026 — a silent rate-limit collapse here is a realistic outage mode. Ultra's 5–10bps is genuinely cheap versus 100bps platforms, so Ultra is a reasonable choice for a NON-latency-sensitive strategy sleeve.

findings.claim: The correct self-hosted architecture builds swap instructions locally with zero RPC round-trips in the hot path; chainstacklabs/pumpfun-bonkfun-bot is the highest-quality open reference
findings.detail: github.com/chainstacklabs/pumpfun-bonkfun-bot (972 stars, 343 forks, Python, actively updated August 2026) is explicitly 'a fully functional pump.fun / letsbonk.fun trading and sniping bot not relying on any 3rd party APIs'. Four listener types with different speed/availability tradeoffs: Geyser (fastest, requires a dedicated Geyser endpoint), Logs (logsSubscribe, works on most providers), Blocks (blockSubscribe, not universally supported), and Pumpportal (third-party aggregator). pump.fun supports all four; letsbonk.fun supports only blocks, geyser and pumpportal. Critical design detail — 'extreme fast mode' executes purchases 'without RPC calls between detecting the token and submitting' by using on-chain CreateEvent data, buying a FIXED token amount rather than querying the bonding curve price first, because 'single account reads typically consume ~40–50ms even on a good endpoint'. The pumpportal listener needs one batched account read (curve + mint) and skips tokens unreadable within curve_refresh_budget (default 2.0 seconds). Config is YAML per bot instance covering buy amount in SOL, slippage, exit strategy, fixed or dynamic priority fees, filters (token age, name/creator matching), retry logic, account cleanup, and token-bucket rate limiting via node.max_rps (default 25). Requires Python 3.11+ and uv; public RPC nodes are explicitly stated to be insufficient. Also credible: github.com/henrytirla/Solana-Trading-Bot (287 stars, Python, solana-py + Jito SDK, Raydium and Pump.fun). Practitioner consensus on the competitive baseline is Yellowstone gRPC streaming plus pre-signed transactions, with ShredStream as the absolute latency floor since it surfaces data as shreds arrive rather than at block boundaries.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Adopt the 'extreme fast mode' pattern as a hard architectural rule: NO account reads between signal detection and transaction submission. Derive everything you need from the streamed CreateEvent payload and buy a fixed token quantity with a wide slippage bound rather than reading the curve to compute an exact price — a single 40–50ms account read is 5% of a 1s budget and is the most common self-inflicted latency leak. Pre-build and pre-sign transaction templates at startup, leaving only the mint address and amount to patch in. Use Yellowstone gRPC, not WebSocket logsSubscribe, for detection. Note node.max_rps default 25 as a sane starting rate-limit and budget for a paid/dedicated RPC from day one. Port the Python reference to Rust only after the strategy is proven — the language is not the bottleneck, the network path is.

findings.claim: Several of the highest-starred GitHub 'Solana sniper bot' repos are hijacked or repurposed pre-Solana repositories and should be treated as malware
findings.detail: GitHub repository search reveals a clear pattern: github.com/mortdeus/solana-copy-sniper-mev-trading-bot has 4,438 stars — by far the most in the category — but a created_at of 2013-03-01, which predates Solana's existence entirely (Solana mainnet launched 2020). Similarly github.com/coffellas-cto/Solana-Copy-Trading-Bot (409 stars) has created_at 2014-12-04, and github.com/WSOL12/Solana-Arbitrage-Bot (516 stars) has created_at 2013-08-29. All three carry heavily keyword-stuffed descriptions with repeated phrases ('solana trading bot solana trading bot solana trading bot', 'Solana Arbitrage Bot' repeated ~11 times) characteristic of SEO manipulation, and one advertises a Telegram contact handle. By contrast the legitimate chainstacklabs/pumpfun-bonkfun-bot was created 2024-09-09, consistent with its subject matter. Reusing an old high-star repository preserves the star count and repo age, both of which are the heuristics developers use to judge trustworthiness — this is a known supply-chain attack pattern for crypto tooling, where the payload typically exfiltrates private keys or seed phrases from .env files.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Hard rule for dependency selection: check created_at against the subject matter before cloning any crypto repo, and reject any 'Solana' repo created before 2020. Reject keyword-stuffed descriptions and repos advertising Telegram contact handles. Never run a sniper repo with a funded .env on a machine that holds real keys — vet in a container with a throwaway key and outbound network egress monitoring first, and grep the full tree for network calls near key material. Prefer repos published under a real company org (chainstacklabs is Chainstack, a known infrastructure vendor) over individual accounts. Star count is actively adversarial as a trust signal in this category.

findings.claim: pump.fun venue fees are 1.25% on the bonding curve and market-cap-tiered on PumpSwap — far higher than the 0.25% figure commonly cited from older sources
findings.detail: Bonding curve (pre-graduation) trades carry 1.25% total, split 0.95% protocol and 0.30% creator. PumpSwap (post-graduation) fees scale DOWN by market cap in SOL: 0–420 SOL → 1.25% (0.93% protocol / 0.30% creator / 0.02% LP); 420–1,470 SOL → 1.20% (0.05% / 0.95% / 0.20%); 1,470–2,460 SOL → 1.15% (0.05% / 0.90% / 0.20%); 2,460–3,440 SOL → 1.10% (0.05% / 0.85% / 0.20%); scaling down gradually to 98,000+ SOL → 0.30% (0.05% protocol / 0.05% creator / 0.20% LP). Coin creation costs 0 SOL; graduation from bonding curve to PumpSwap carries a fixed 0.015 SOL fee inclusive of network fees. Fee sharing lets creators split accumulated fees among up to 10 shareholders via the PumpFees program, on both bonding-curve and graduated AMM tokens. For comparison, Raydium CLMM fee tiers are 0.02%, 0.03%, 0.04% and 2%, while Raydium CPMM tiers are 1%, 2% and 4%; Raydium CLMM pools can enable dynamic fees applying a volatility-driven surcharge on top of the base rate using a mechanism derived from the Trader Joe / Meteora dynamic-fee design. Meteora DLMM uses discrete bins rather than a continuous tick curve and applies dynamic fees that rise during volatility. Note the widely-repeated '0.25% PumpSwap fee' from the March 2025 launch coverage is now stale.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Hardcode 1.25% as the bonding-curve venue fee in your P&L model, not 0.25% — getting this wrong understates round-trip cost by 200bps and will make a losing strategy backtest as profitable. Implement PumpSwap fees as a market-cap lookup table rather than a constant, since the spread between the 0–420 SOL tier (1.25%) and the 98k+ tier (0.30%) is 95bps and materially changes which exits are worth taking. The tiering has a strategy implication: early small-cap exits are expensive, so factor the fee decay into hold-versus-exit logic. For Raydium, detect the actual pool type before modeling — assuming 0.25% AMM v4 when you are actually trading a 1% or 2% CPMM launchpad pool is a 75–175bp error per side.

findings.claim: Alpenglow's 150ms finality is NOT live as of August 2026 — build against the current 400ms slot
findings.detail: Solana's Alpenglow upgrade replaces TowerBFT and Proof-of-History consensus with Votor (a voting layer moving validator votes off-chain) and Rotor (a new block propagation engine), targeting roughly 150ms finality down from about 12.8 seconds under TowerBFT, and freeing an estimated 75% of block space currently consumed by vote transactions. Validators approved SIMD-0326 with 98.27% support in September 2025. The upgrade entered live community validator testing in May 2026. Official guidance points to Agave 4.3 and an OCTOBER 2026 mainnet activation. It is therefore not active as of August 2026. SOURCE DISAGREEMENT: at least one vendor blog (rpcfast.com) writes as though Alpenglow is already shipped, stating 'finality after Alpenglow lands in 150ms' and that 'bots optimized for the old 400ms slot rhythm are now systematically late' — this is incorrect as of the research date and appears to be forward-dated marketing copy. Current slot time remains ~400ms.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Build and tune against a 400ms slot today, but parameterize slot duration and finality assumptions as configuration rather than constants, because an October 2026 activation will compress the sniping window and invalidate any hardcoded timing. Specifically: any logic of the form 'wait N slots before confirming' or 'retry after 400ms' must read from config. Schedule a re-tuning cycle for the Agave 4.3 rollout and expect competitive tip levels to reprice at that point. Treat vendor blogs as unreliable on network-upgrade status and verify against solana.com/upgrades/alpenglow or validator governance records.

findings.claim: Peer-reviewed survival analysis of 832,941 pump.fun launches gives directly usable, statistically validated pre-trade filters
findings.detail: arXiv 2607.02823 / SSRN 6915560, 'Pump.fun Graduation Regime Windows: Survival Analysis of 832,941 Token Launches and the Social-Presence Effect' (Arati Uday Kamat), covering launches between 8 May and 10 June 2026. Fast-regime pooled graduation rate 0.198% (95% CI 0.189%–0.208%); steady-state 0.207%; authors note this is a lower bound, not a full 24-hour estimate. SOCIAL PRESENCE: launches advertising a Telegram channel graduate at 1.485% versus 0.166% without — an 8.94x lift, Cox hazard ratio 5.40 (95% CI [4.73, 6.17]). Launches advertising all three social channels graduate at 1.919% versus 0.110% for launches with none — a 17.4x lift. STRONGEST SINGLE PREDICTOR: initial market capitalization above the 30 SOL platform default, Cox HR 4.51, with the top quartile achieving a 0.634% graduation rate. Model quality: Cox concordance 0.858, stable under bootstrap and a time-window split. Dataset of 860,213 launches released CC-BY-4.0 via Zenodo. Corroborating base rates from other sources: DEXTools reports the graduation rate fell to ~0.26% by mid-June 2026, versus 0.63% in September–October 2025 (a 3.18x decline); a CoinGecko study found only ~5% of pump.fun tokens survive past 90 days; and of 18.67M tokens launched January 2024–June 2026, 4.55% remained actively traded beyond 90 days while 68.67% recorded their last trade on the same day they launched.
findings.actionable_for_bot: These are the most valuable numbers in this research because they are peer-reviewed with confidence intervals rather than vendor claims. Implement as hard pre-trade gates: (1) REQUIRE a Telegram link in token metadata — this alone is an 8.94x improvement in graduation odds and eliminates the majority of launches at near-zero cost; (2) prefer all-three-socials tokens (17.4x lift over none); (3) REQUIRE initial market cap strictly above the 30 SOL platform default, the single strongest predictor at HR 4.51. Applying all three should lift your candidate pool's base rate from ~0.2% toward the 1.9%+ range. Equally important for sizing: even a well-filtered candidate has under a 2% graduation probability, so the strategy must be structured as many small positions with an aggressive stop, never as conviction bets. The 68.67% same-day-death statistic argues for a hard time-based exit measured in minutes to hours. Download the CC-BY-4.0 Zenodo dataset to backtest your own filter stack against 860,213 labeled launches rather than guessing.

findings.claim: RugCheck and PumpPortal provide cheap, usable safety and data primitives, but RugCheck's rate limit puts it outside the hot path
findings.detail: RugCheck: public REST API at api.rugcheck.xyz documented via Swagger, endpoint pattern /tokens/scan/{chain}/{contractAddress}. Returns creator details (address, balance), token supply and distribution (top holders, insider status), liquidity market info, a RugCheck score and a list of identified risks. Auth via a per-developer X-API-KEY header, or 'RugCheck Standard Login' by signing a Solana message. RATE LIMITS: unauthenticated 10 reports per minute; authenticated 60 per minute. Read endpoints are publicly accessible without a key. PumpPortal: 0.5% fee on each Local trade (you sign and submit yourself) and 1% on each Lightning trade (they handle submission). WebSocket data feed at wss://pumpportal.fun/api/data with four streams — subscribeNewToken (free), subscribeMigration (free), subscribeTokenTrade (metered at 0.01 SOL per 10,000 events) and subscribeAccountTrade (same rate). Solana Tracker Data API pricing: Free €0/mo (2,500 requests/month, 3 rps), €50/mo (200,000 requests, no rate limit), €200/mo (1,000,000 requests), €397/mo (10,000,000 requests plus Datastream WebSocket access); 30% discount on annual billing. Commonly cited safety heuristics across sniper tooling: mint authority, freeze authority, top-10 holder concentration, liquidity lock, honeypot simulation, deployer wallet history, dev wallet concentration, LP burn status, bundle detection, buy/sell tax, social presence and metadata validation.
findings.actionable_for_bot: RugCheck at 60 requests/minute authenticated is one request per second — usable for a confirmation pass or a watchlist pre-warm, but NOT inside a <1s hot path where you may see dozens of launches per second. Correct pattern: compute mint authority, freeze authority and LP burn checks yourself directly from streamed account data (they are simple account-flag reads you already have from the Geyser payload), and use RugCheck asynchronously for post-entry position validation and for offline filter calibration. PumpPortal's free subscribeNewToken and subscribeMigration streams are a genuinely cheap detection fallback and a good redundancy layer behind your primary Geyser feed, but its Local-trade 0.5% fee is pure margin loss versus self-constructing the same instruction for 0%. Note the specific holder-concentration threshold numbers were not verifiable in this research — the 12-point checklists come from paid press-release content (openpr.com) and vendor marketing, so calibrate your own concentration cutoff against the Zenodo dataset rather than adopting a quoted figure.

Chainstack reference bot's default token-bucket rate limit against the RPC node. Reasonable starting point; public RPCs are explicitly insufficient for this workload.

traps_and_failure_modes: BullX dependency is now a worked example of total platform risk: it suspended all trading on 1 June 2026 with no warning, no timeline and no airdrop after collecting a reported $200M+ in fees. Any architecture routing execution through a third-party frontend can be zeroed overnight. This is the strongest single argument for the self-hosted path.

Almost every retail platform in this landscape (Photon, Axiom, Trojan, Bloom, Nova, Vector, Padre, Pepeboost, BonkBot, Banana Gun, Maestro) has NO public trading API. Driving them means Telegram userbot automation or browser scraping — both are ToS violations, both break on every UI change, and both add hundreds of milliseconds that make a <1s budget impossible. Photon explicitly warns that third-party automation scripts should be considered unsafe.

GMGN is the tempting trap: it has a real API, so it looks like the answer, but one call per 5 seconds means you cannot even fetch a route fast enough for a single signal, let alone a stream of them. Do not discover this after building against it.

Jupiter Ultra looks like the obvious managed solution and is genuinely well-built, but its own published numbers (/order 300ms P50, /execute 700ms–2s) exceed a 1s end-to-end budget before the transaction is even broadcast. Use Swap V2/Metis to build instructions and submit them yourself instead.

Alpenglow's 150ms finality is NOT live — it targets Agave 4.3 / October 2026. At least one vendor blog states it as already shipped and claims bots tuned for 400ms slots are 'now systematically late'. Building against phantom network parameters will mis-tune every timing constant you have.

Hijacked GitHub repos are actively distributing malware in this exact niche. The single highest-starred 'Solana sniper' repo (4,438 stars) has a created_at of 2013 — years before Solana existed. Two other high-star repos date to 2013 and 2014. Old repos are recycled precisely because star count and repo age are the trust heuristics developers use. Never run one with a funded .env.

Any account read between signal detection and submission costs ~40–50ms even on a good endpoint — roughly 5% of a 1s budget. Reading the bonding curve to compute an exact price before buying is the most common self-inflicted latency leak. Buy a fixed token quantity from streamed CreateEvent data with a wide slippage bound instead.

Jito's 1 request/second per IP per region limit silently throttles bursty strategies. During a launch wave you will exceed it instantly and get 429s. Fan out across all 8 mainnet regional endpoints and/or request a raised limit before you need it.

Helius Sender rejects any transaction missing EITHER the SOL tip transfer OR the setComputeUnitPrice instruction. This is an easy omission that manifests as a total submission failure under load rather than a clear error at build time.

The 0.001 SOL minimum tip on Sender Max and Nozomi is ~200x the observed median landed tip (5e-6 SOL) and exceeds even the 99th percentile (7.02e-4 SOL). Paying it indiscriminately on every trade — including uncontested exits — is a large and completely avoidable cost. Gate the tier by contested-ness.

Tip and priority fees are fixed in SOL and do not scale with position size, so they silently destroy small trades: ~0.0012 SOL of fixed cost is 1.2% of a 0.1 SOL trade but 0.024% of a 5 SOL trade. Enforce a minimum viable trade size (~0.5 SOL) or the fee floor eats the strategy.

Modeling pump.fun at the widely-repeated 0.25% is a 100bp-per-side error — the bonding curve is 1.25% and PumpSwap starts at 1.25% for sub-420-SOL market caps. Similarly, assuming Raydium's legacy 0.25% AMM v4 on what is actually a 1%/2%/4% CPMM launchpad pool understates cost by 75–375bp per side. A backtest built on stale fee constants will show profit where none exists.

Axiom's February 2026 insider scandal is a strategy-leakage risk, not a custody risk: employees used an over-permissive admin dashboard to inspect prominent traders' private wallet activity. For a systematic bot, an operator observing your entry pattern can copy or front-run it, degrading alpha silently and invisibly. Non-custodial does not mean unobserved.

Maestro is genuinely custodial — keys are generated and held on their infrastructure — and permits only a SINGLE mnemonic export. Banana Gun and Photon also allow only one-time key export. Miss that one export and the wallet is permanently platform-locked.

Banana Gun's September 2024 exploit drained ~$3M from 11 wallets and specifically targeted 'smart money' via manual transfers rather than an automated drain. Being a profitable, identifiable bot operator raises rather than lowers your targeting risk on any custodial or semi-custodial surface.

Jupiter's legacy portal rate-limit grandfathering expired 30 June 2026. If billing was never set up on the new Developer Platform, rate limits can collapse without an obvious error — a realistic silent outage mode.

'Sub-millisecond execution' (Bloom v2.0) is physically impossible for on-chain settlement on a 400ms-slot chain. Treat all vendor speed claims in this category as marketing, and every RPC-vendor benchmark as sales material — RPC Fast's '10% of bots profit / 90% fail on latency' figures come from a company selling latency.

The base rates are the real risk, not the infrastructure: a 0.198% graduation rate means even a well-filtered candidate has under a 2% chance of graduating, and 68.67% of tokens die the same day they launch. A stack that fires in 200ms into unfiltered launches simply loses money faster. Position sizing and hard time-based exits matter more than shaving another 20ms.

Sources conflict on effective fees for several platforms (Padre/Terminal: 0.8% vs 35% cashback; MEVx: 0.8% vs 0.9–1%; Trojan: 0.5% vs 0.55% vs 0.75%). Axiom's cashback tier volume thresholds are entirely unpublished — one source explicitly warns that any guide quoting a dollar threshold is guessing. Do not encode these as facts.
No substantive fee, custody or API data could be located for Vector in this research. Treat it as unverified rather than assuming it matches the 1% cohort.

Specific holder-concentration thresholds (e.g. 'reject if top-10 non-LP holders exceed X%') could not be verified from any credible source — the 12-point safety checklists circulating come from paid press releases (openpr.com) and vendor marketing. Calibrate your own cutoff against the CC-BY-4.0 Zenodo dataset of 860,213 labeled launches rather than adopting a quoted number.

Solana low-latency execution infrastruct.topic: Solana low-latency execution infrastructure for a memecoin sniping/trading bot: providers, priority fees, Jito tips, compute budgets, detection paths, landing rates, colocation, and MEV/sandwich risk on buys
Solana low-latency execution infrastruct.executive_summary: URGENT, TIME-CRITICAL: Jito ShredStream is deprecated and shuts down 2026-09-05 — 13 days from today (2026-08-23). If your design assumes ShredStream, it is already dead. Jito's own docs point to DoubleZero Edge (multicast shreds, $30–100 USDC per device per epoch ≈ $450–1,500/mo); OrbitFlare ShredStream and AllenHark Shreds are drop-in raw-UDP alternatives. Second structural change: SIMD-0286 raised the block limit from 60M to 100M CU on 2026-07-29 (epoch 1009), but the 12M CU per-writable-account-per-block cap was NOT raised — that cap, not the block cap, is what throttles you when 500 bots hit the same pump.fun bonding curve. At ~80k CU per buy, roughly 150 buys can land per block against one curve; everything else is dropped regardless of fee. I measured live tip and CU data rather than quoting blogs. Jito tip floor on 2026-08-23 (three samples, 13 min apart) was p50 3,511–6,602 lamports, p75 7,128–41,750 lamports, p95 92,676–750,000 lamports — note the p75 swung 6x and p95 swung 8x within thirteen minutes, so any hardcoded tip is wrong within minutes; poll https://bundles.jito.wtf/api/v1/bundles/tip_floor or the tip_stream websocket. SOL was $95.27, so the p95 tip is ~$0.071 — trivially cheap relative to a snipe, which means tip is not your cost constraint and you should bid aggressively (p95–p99, 100k–750k lamports) for contested launches. I measured compute units from real mainnet transactions: pump.fun bonding-curve buy = 58,887–91,305 CU when the ATA already exists, ~102,351 CU when the buy creates the ATA; pump.fun sell = 64,931–73,938 CU; PumpSwap bare swap = 21,125–21,686 CU (very tight cluster), 26,160–59,172 CU with ATA/wSOL handling; Raydium AMM v4 swap = 48,200 CU and 53,631 CU in two tight clusters. Nearly every bot on chain over-requests: I saw CU limits of 400,000 and 1,400,000 set on transactions that consumed 135k. Over-requesting wastes nothing in fees (you pay on requested CU × price, so it directly overpays) and worsens your block-packing position — set the limit to measured p95 + ~20%, not 200k/400k defaults. On detection: Yellowstone/Dragon's Mouth gRPC beats WebSocket decisively — Triton's own published measurement is slot updates p90 ~5ms via gRPC vs ~150ms via RPC polling, and account updates p90 ~215ms via gRPC vs ~374ms via native WebSocket. Helius LaserStream's preprocessed shred delivery claims ~8ms ahead of the `processed` commitment. logsSubscribe is the worst option and should not be in a production snipe path. Colocation is not optional: Europe produces 68.5% of leader slots (Frankfurt 19–26%, Amsterdam 16–25%, London 12%), TeraSwitch hosts ~59% of validators, and the lowest measured QUIC handshake to a validator is 965µs from an in-datacenter probe versus 60–75ms from AWS Ashburn to New Jersey and 190–220ms Singapore-to-EU. A US-hosted bot loses the race on physics before any code runs. On MEV: sandwiching is real and memecoin-concentrated — 16 of the top 20 sandwiched tokens were pump.fun tokens, ~51,600 attacks/day at 88.9% success, average extraction 0.0425 SOL ($8.67 at the time of that report) per attack. Your slippage cap IS the attacker's budget: 1% slippage on a $10,000 buy hands over up to $100. The single highest-leverage mitigation is not a wider slippage number but computing an exact minAmountOut from the bonding-curve/pool reserve state you already read at detection time, then submitting via a Jito bundle (never publicly broadcast) or a private relay. Sources materially disagree on three points I flag below: Helius Sender's minimum tip (docs say 0.001 SOL, Helius's own blog and the widely-used sol-trade-sdk say 0.0002 SOL), 0slot's minimum tip (0.001 SOL on lower tiers, 0.0001 only on Advanced — the SDK hardcodes 0.0001 and will get your transactions silently dropped), and whether priority fees/Jito tips help at all (Chorus One's Nov-2024 study says negligible; that study measured ordinary 90-second-window transactions, not same-slot auctions, and does not generalize to sniping).

findings.detail: Jito's own docs at docs.jito.wtf/lowlatencytxnfeed/ carry a DEPRECATED banner: complete shutdown 2026-09-05, no further access. Today is 2026-08-23 — 13 days of runway. findings.claim: DoubleZero Edge delivers shreds via multicast, ~28ms faster than Jito ShredStream at p95, priced per device per epoch
findings.detail: Pricing: $30–$100 USDC per device per epoch; a Solana epoch is ~2 days, so ~15 epochs/month = ~$450–$1,500/month per device, varying by metro. findings.claim: Measured compute units actually consumed by pump.fun, PumpSwap and Raydium swaps on mainnet
findings.detail:
I sampled real successful mainnet transactions via getTransaction and read meta.computeUnitsConsumed, classifying by Anchor discriminator and ATA-program presence.
pump.fun bonding curve BUY, no ATA creation: 58,887 / 76,729 / 85,746 / 91,305 CU observed.
pump.fun BUY with ATA creation in the tx: 102,351 CU (router-wrapped variants ran 216k-231k).
pump.fun SELL, no ATA creation: 64,931 / 69,074 / 72,035 / 72,417 / 73,938 CU.
PumpSwap AMM bare swap (3 top-level ix): 21,125 / 21,125 / 21,125 / 21,198 / 21,686 / 21,686 CU — extremely tight cluster. With ATA/wSOL handling (4 ix): 26,160 / 48,387 / 52,256 / 59,172 CU.
Raydium AMM v4 swap (4 top-level ix): two tight clusters at 48,200-48,201 CU (n=5) and 53,631 CU (n=7).
Observed CU *limits* that bots actually set were wildly oversized: p50 400,000 and up to 1,400,000 on pump.fun txs that consumed 135k; Raydium bots cluster on a 320,000 limit for a 48-54k CU swap.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Set ComputeBudgetProgram.setComputeUnitLimit precisely: pump.fun buy w/ existing ATA = 110,000; pump.fun buy creating ATA = 140,000; pump.fun sell = 95,000; PumpSwap bare swap = 40,000; PumpSwap w/ ATA = 90,000; Raydium AMM v4 swap = 75,000. These are measured p95 + ~20% headroom. Because the prioritization fee is ceil(cu_price × cu_limit / 1e6), a 320,000 limit on a 48,000 CU swap overpays the priority fee by 6.7x for zero benefit. Simulate once per route on startup and cache the limit rather than guessing.

findings.claim: The 12M CU per-writable-account-per-block cap — not the block cap — is the real sniping bottleneck, and it did not move when the block cap rose 66%
findings.detail: SIMD-0286 activated on mainnet 2026-07-29 at epoch 1009, raising max block compute from 60M to 100M CU (+66%). The maximum compute that may write to any single account within one block remains 12,000,000 CU, unchanged. Max block accounts-data-size delta remains 100MB. Per-transaction max is 1,400,000 CU; default per-instruction budget is 200,000 CU; builtin instructions default to 3,000 CU. Base fee is 5,000 lamports per signature, split 50/50 burn/validator. Prioritization fee = ceil(compute_unit_price × compute_unit_limit / 1,000,000) lamports. I verified epoch length live: slotsInEpoch = 432,000 (epoch 1021, absoluteSlot 441,185,271).
findings.actionable_for_bot: A pump.fun bonding curve is a single writable account. At ~80,000 CU per buy, only ~150 buy transactions can land against that one curve per block (12M / 80k), regardless of what anyone pays. This means: (1) minimizing your CU limit literally increases the number of slots-worth of competitors you beat, since the cap is consumed in requested-CU order by the scheduler; (2) if you are not in the first ~150 accepted txs you do not land — no tip fixes it; (3) plan for slot-1 and slot-2 fallback entries with recomputed pricing rather than assuming slot-0 or nothing.

findings.claim: Yellowstone/Dragon's Mouth gRPC beats WebSocket and polling by measured, published margins
findings.detail: Triton One's own published figures for Dragon's Mouth: slot updates p90 ~5ms via gRPC vs ~150ms for standard RPC polling; account updates p90 ~215ms via gRPC vs ~374ms via native RPC WebSockets. gRPC uses Protobuf binary with native HTTP/2 flow control and backpressure; JSON-RPC WebSocket has none. Triton bandwidth pricing ~$0.08/GB vs Helius ~$0.15/GB equivalent. Secondary sources put gRPC at sub-100ms vs 200-400ms for WebSocket subscriptions, and one cites ~5ms gRPC vs ~150ms JSON-RPC/WebSocket. Helius LaserStream is wire-compatible with Yellowstone gRPC and adds historical replay of up to 216,000 slots (~24h), auto-reconnect with replay, multi-node failover, and token-account (ATA-expansion) filtering. LaserStream shred delivery in preprocessed mode claims data ~8ms ahead of the `processed` commitment level; preprocessed transactions cost 2 credits per 0.1 MB uncompressed.
findings.actionable_for_bot: Use gRPC transaction streams with commitment=processed as the baseline detection path; use logsSubscribe only as a cold-standby health check, never in the hot path. The account-update p90 of ~215ms is the number that matters and it is a big fraction of a 400ms slot — this is exactly why shreds (DoubleZero/OrbitFlare) exist and why gRPC alone will not win contested slot-0 launches. Design a two-tier ingest: shreds for the trigger, gRPC for confirmation/state reconciliation.

findings.claim: Colocation region determines whether you can compete at all; Europe produces ~68.5% of leader slots
findings.detail: Glassnode's Solana latency map probes QUIC handshake latency from worldwide probes to all ~760 active validators. Lowest measured handshake: 965µs (0.965ms) in Chicago, i.e. same-datacenter colocation. Amsterdam alone produces ~25% of leader slots (April 2026 data); TeraSwitch Networks hosts ~59% of validators and produces ~59% of leader slots, and Jito's regional block engines run on TeraSwitch too. A separate Glassnode figure attributes 68.5% of the 432,000 leader slots in epoch 1006 to Europe (~296,000 slots). City stake shares reported at Frankfurt 19-25.9%, Amsterdam 16-21%, London 12-12.4%. Measured route latencies: Hetzner Falkenstein → Solana Frankfurt 1.2ms; AWS Frankfurt → Solana Frankfurt 1.5-2.5ms; GCP Amsterdam → Solana Amsterdam 3.5ms; AWS Ashburn → Solana New Jersey 60-75ms; AWS Singapore → EU clusters 190-220ms. Leader rotation is every 1.6s (4 consecutive 400ms slots). Note the caveat Glassnode itself gives: QUIC handshake latency measures network distance, not end-to-end inclusion, which also depends on SWQoS (80% of capacity reserved for staked connections).
findings.actionable_for_bot: Deploy in Frankfurt or Amsterdam bare metal, ideally TeraSwitch or a facility with sub-2ms to the local validator cluster. Do not run a competitive sniper from us-east AWS: 60-75ms one way is ~15-19% of a slot burned before your packet exists. If you must have US presence, run it as a separate strategy (larger caps, later entries), not as the snipe path. Budget ~$1,200-2,900/mo for suitable bare metal; one source quotes dedicated Solana-adjacent bare metal at $2,200/mo with 72h delivery.

findings.claim: Helius Sender: free, tip-only, dual-routes to Jito + SWQoS + Harmonic + Rakurai, 50 TPS default, 7 regional endpoints
